title: No algorithmic rent setting rule at the state level
citation: Mass. Bill S.2983 (194th General Court), Bill History
requirement: Massachusetts algorithmic rent-setting legislation exists only as pending bills (S.2983 and H.5222) reported by the Joint Committee on Housing on 3/12/2026 and referred to Ways and Means; no enacted state rule is shown.

title: No rent increase limits rule at the city level
requirement: Massachusetts law (c. 40P, s. 4) bars cities from enacting or enforcing rent control (aside from a narrow voluntary opt-in exception); Boston's home-rule petition H.3744 is only a bill, and the statewide ballot question was struck.

source.quote: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind

title: No just cause eviction rule at the city level
requirement: Boston's tenant eviction protections exist only as a home rule petition (H.3744) seeking state authorization; the excerpted bill history shows only committee referral and reporting-date extensions, with no enactment. The city's adopted ordinance (HSNA) only requires notice of rights and does not halt evictions, so no city-level just cause eviction rule is shown.

source.quote: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
